Samsung releases world's first 2TB consumer SSDs
Expensive right now, but I'm excited for these and other models to become cheaper. This should also force other SSD manufacturers to create their own 2tb drives.
One should note that the 2TB version is slightly cheaper(per GB) than the 1TB version. I expect the 2TB version to drop in price soon after launch though.
That is an oddity. Usually it is the otherway around, especially for newer technology.

I haven't been paying too much attention, but the part I noticed was the 5 or 10 year warranty on these new SSD's. Considering that their lifespan was closer to 2 years maybe a year or two ago, seeing a 10 year warranty is very surprising. And the price is slowly going down. Slowly.

I can't wait to deploy these in the small/midsize business server space, with vmware HA failover "consumer" grade SSDs are more than fine, they already fail less than the enterprise HDDs in place. Arrays of these will be amazing, so reasonably priced too.

The thing I'm going to be listening for the next time I go into a server room is the noise. HDD's make a racket. Once these things are fully deployed everywhere, the only sounds left in a server room will be the fans/coolers. Sure they make the most racket, but even they're starting to see other cooling solutions that are more efficient.
